results.label: this tree ships the M12 rule-break tally (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the analytics payload carries the tally beside the other read-only aggregates
an empty but readable audit is a real ZERO with its own shape — not the unavailable shape
the tally reports the account scope it used, so the review can state what it covers
the endpoint publishes its limits: read-only, no writes, no grade/cap/permission/decision influence, no causal claim
reading the tally twice writes NOTHING: every table is byte-identical, including the audit it reads
the tally counts what the endpoint’s own account recorded: three attempts (two prevented, one accepted override) and one observed stop
the rules are NAMED, so the review can say which one fired
another account of the same trader is NOT folded in: the second desk’s blocked attempt on the news rule is absent here
and that other account reports its own tally when it is the account being reviewed
the default (no account_id) review scopes the tally to the account IT resolved, so the payload never disagrees with itself
another trader’s audit rows are excluded from every number the endpoint returns
the window the caller asked for is applied to the audit’s own days
seeding rule breaks changes NO performance number in the same payload: the whole statistics block is byte-identical with and without them
and so is the account block: the tally cannot move a balance, a cap or a policy field
no grade, score or permission is derived from the tally anywhere in its own payload
a reversed range is UNKNOWN, not zero and not a clean week, and the rest of the review still answers with a 200
an account the trader does not own is never read: the payload falls back to their own desk and the foreign id appears in no scope
the tally is not readable without a session, like the rest of the payload
a bounded read takes the MOST RECENT events (the newest two are a legal record and an observed stop, so they are what must come back) and reports the truncation instead of hiding rows
one more row of budget reaches the newest attempt, so the bound is a window and not a filter
an unreadable store is UNKNOWN for the endpoint too: the failure is not reported as zero breaks
the audit rows the probe seeded are still exactly what it wrote: seeding is the app’s own shape, not a probe fiction

scope: M12 api: recorded rule breaks, scoped and read-only: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
